metadata.note: East Tennessee and Western North Carolina Railroad ('Tweetsie', 3 ft gauge) Johnson City, TN - Cranberry, NC, and the Linville River Railway Cranberry - Pineola / Boone, NC, which it ran as one system 1913-1940; plus the Linville River Railway's own Ritter-era trains 1909-1913 as a separate operator feature. The ET&WNC main line is split where passenger service ended at different times: Johnson City - Port Rayon 1881-1934 [OPEN], Port Rayon - Elizabethton 1881-1943 [OPEN], Elizabethton - Hampton 1881-1950, Hampton - Cranberry 1882-1950; the LRR pieces are Cranberry - Montezuma 1913-1940, Montezuma - Pineola 1913-1933 [OPEN] and Montezuma - Boone 1919-1940 (report blocks [7] Montezuma - Shulls Mills and [8] Shulls Mills - Boone, grouped because both draw 1919-1940). Drawn spans follow the report's drawable: fields exactly. Research report: research/branches/east_tennessee_and_western_north_carolina_railroad.txt.
metadata.operator_split: Rule 4 split at the April 1913 sale of the Linville River Railway by W. M. Ritter to the Cranberry Iron & Coal / ET&WNC group: lrr-cranberry-pineola (Linville River Railway, Ritter era, 1909-1913) in its own colour #A6218B on geometry identical to etwnc-cranberry-montezuma + etwnc-montezuma-pineola. From 1913 the LRR remained a separate reporting corporation but had the ET&WNC's officers and ran through trains Johnson City - Boone, so its 1913-1940 trains are drawn as ET&WNC features in the ET&WNC colour #328C1C with notes naming the LRR as owner (the report's recommendation). NOT a split: Cranberry Iron & Coal control of the ET&WNC itself, continuous 1879-1950 (no lease, receivership or Class I operation found). Both colours are new; a script confirmed no other company in data/ uses either.
not_yet_sourced: OPEN ENDS: etwnc-johnson-city-port-rayon ends at 1934 [OPEN] (last confirmed: NCCC order No. 84, trains 1 and 2 Johnson City - Boone); the real cutback is somewhere 1934-1943 ('post-war' per etwncrrhs.org conflicts mildly with the 1943 timetable already starting at Port Rayon). etwnc-port-rayon-elizabethton ends at 1943 [OPEN] (1943 public timetable via Fowler); by Oct 1950 trains started at Elizabethton. etwnc-montezuma-pineola ends at 1933 [OPEN] (1933 Official Guide via Fowler); actual end 1933-1940. Best next sources: a Tennessee PUC / ICC discontinuance order, Johnson City Press and Elizabethton Star files, Mallory Hope Ferrell 'Tweetsie Country' (1976), 1935-1950 Official Guides.
OPEN START: lrr-cranberry-pineola starts at 1909 [OPEN] (first NCCC return printing passengers); the 1906-1908 returns were not checked.
Withheld start: Montezuma - Shulls Mills may have carried passengers from 1916/17 (opening; 1917 passenger revenue jump) - drawn only from the confirmed May 9, 1919 Boone service.
Fowler's ET&WNC legend is internally inconsistent ('b: 1933G' with no station lettered b; 'c:' with no year); nothing drawn here depends on it.
Last ET&WNC passenger day: Sept 24, 1950 (HMDB marker via snippet) vs Oct 12 / 16 / 19, 1950 - year 1950 safe.

Source conflict recorded, not adopted: american-rails.com says the ET&WNC never ran scheduled passenger trains year-round, only in summer - contradicted by the NCCC passenger counts (150,271 in 1924), the 1934 order and the WWII seven-day worker trains.

Boone opening conflict: 1919 drawn (NCCC 1919, Appalachian State May 9, 1919, Boone survey) vs 1918 (construction/freight train) vs one 1916 outlier; the Boone depot's '1917-1940' (Clio marker) is not used.
All headway_min and avg_speed_kmh values are estimates; no dated timetable was read.
Several sources (Appalachian State note, Watauga Democrat 1940 and 1952, Boone survey, HMDB marker) were read only through search snippets; DigitalNC and HMDB were unreachable during research.
omitted: [9] ET&WNC Buffalo Bridge - Smalling branch, TN (2.00 mi in NCCC road operated 1916-1920): drawable NONE - no passenger evidence of any kind, location not established; probably an industrial / lumber spur (Rule 1).
[10] Linville River Railway Minneapolis Junction branch, NC: drawable NONE - no passenger evidence, destination unverified (Rule 1).

Would be its own company, not ET&WNC.
[12] reserved placeholder in the report (see [6a], drawn here as lrr-cranberry-pineola).

[13] Tweetsie Railroad theme park loop near Blowing Rock, NC (1957-): out of scope - an amusement ride on a site the ET&WNC never reached; not ET&WNC service. Also not drawn: ET&WNC No. 12 on the Shenandoah Central at Penn Laird, VA, 1953-54.
[14] Pre-1879 broad-gauge ET&WNC (No. 1): graded 1868-70, never operated - nothing to draw.

segments.note: ET&WNC narrow-gauge main line, Johnson City - Sinking Creek - Milligan College - Watauga Point - Sycamore Shoals (Gladeland) - Port Rayon (Bemberg). Opened with the Johnson City - Hampton line on Aug 22, 1881 (ICC valuation; passenger service from opening is stated by every secondary history but no 1881 timetable was seen). The first ~10 mi were three-rail dual gauge so standard-gauge freight could reach the rayon plants. End: [OPEN] 1934. NC Corporation Commission Utilities Commission order No. 84 (Jan-Oct 1934) changed the schedules of 'trains No. 1 and 2 between Johnson City, Tenn., and Boone, N.C.' - trains still left Johnson City in 1934. This is the last CONFIRMED year, not a known end - no source dates when service actually stopped. Do not extend without evidence. The cutback lies somewhere 1934-1943: Fowler's 1943 public timetable letter (d) starts at Port Rayon and omits Johnson City, Milligan College, Watauga Point and Sycamore Shoals (absence evidence only); etwncrrhs.org says 'post-war, the narrow gauge was cut back to Elizabethton - Cranberry'; an undated late-1930s compiled Johnson City list still shows ET&WNC departures. After 1950 the section was standard-gauge FREIGHT only (ET&WNC, 'Freight Service only' in the Feb 1952 Official Guide; then East Tennessee Railway to 2003/2005) - not drawn (Rule 1). headway_min 360 is an ESTIMATE from 'three daily round-trip passenger runs' in the line's busier years (bcyesteryear summary of Trains, Jan 1951; era not stated); no dated timetable was read.
sources: Segment-level: ICC valuation abstract (opened Aug 22, 1881 - start); NC Corporation Commission 1934 report, Utilities Commission order No. 84 (trains 1 and 2 Johnson City - Boone, last confirmed year, [OPEN]); Fowler tennesseerrs.pdf line 82 (1943 timetable starts at Port Rayon - absence evidence, not used as an end). Headway not sourced.

segments.note: ET&WNC main line, Port Rayon - Elizabethton. Opened Aug 22, 1881 with the Johnson City - Hampton line (ICC valuation). Kept separate because the 1943 public timetable (Fowler letter d) began at Port Rayon ('d(tm)', Elizabethton 'd') - WWII shift trains carried rayon workers from the mountains to the Bemberg / North American Rayon plants seven days a week (etwncrrhs.org). End: [OPEN] 1943. This is the last CONFIRMED year, not a known end - no source dates when service actually stopped. Do not extend without evidence. By Oct 1950 the last run started and ended at Elizabethton (Trains, Jan 1951, via bcyesteryear), so trains had stopped reaching Port Rayon by then; when is unknown (1943-1950). segments.note: Linville River Railway as part of the ET&WNC system: Cranberry - Minneapolis Junction - Minneapolis - Vale - Newland (Avery County seat) - Montezuma. Owned by the Linville River Railway Company - a separate corporation filing its own NC Corporation Commission returns with its own crews - but bought by the Cranberry Iron & Coal / ET&WNC group in April 1913 and run from then as one system with the ET&WNC under identical officers at Johnson City, with through trains Johnson City - Boone (1934 order, trains 1 and 2). Drawn in the ET&WNC colour as the company that ran the trains (Rule 4). Start 1913: CI&C bought the LRR from W. M. Ritter in April 1913 (etwncrrhs.org; Wikipedia); passenger trains ran on this track earlier under Ritter - see lrr-cranberry-pineola. NCCC returns print LRR revenue passengers through the period (23,268 in FY1915/16; 78,803 in 1919; 37,355 in 1924 or 1925; about 4,325 in 1932). End: the flood of Aug 13, 1940 put the whole Cranberry - Boone line out of commission and service never resumed (Appalachian State collection note); the LRR petitioned to abandon and the ICC approved in 1941 (March 22 per Wikipedia; May 22 per another result - irrelevant to the drawn years). headway_min 720 is an ESTIMATE: the undated late-1930s Johnson City list shows about two trains each way (Johnson City - Boone and Johnson City - Pineola with connection to Boone); no dated timetable was read.

Headway not sourced.

segments.note: Linville River Railway (ET&WNC system), Montezuma - Love's Crossing (flag) - Pineola (ex-Saginaw; post office renamed 1914). The ORIGINAL end of the line at Ritter's Saginaw band mill; from 1919 the Boone line left at Montezuma and Pineola became a short branch. NCCC 'road operated' kept listing Cranberry - Pineola through 1934. Owned by the Linville River Railway Company - a separate corporation filing its own NC Corporation Commission returns with its own crews - but bought by the Cranberry Iron & Coal / ET&WNC group in April 1913 and run from then as one system with the ET&WNC under identical officers at Johnson City, with through trains Johnson City - Boone (1934 order, trains 1 and 2). Drawn in the ET&WNC colour as the company that ran the trains (Rule 4). Start 1913 (CI&C purchase, as etwnc-cranberry-montezuma). End: [OPEN] 1933 - Pineola is lettered c = 1933 Official Guide in Fowler. This is the last CONFIRMED year, not a known end - no source dates when service actually stopped. Do not extend without evidence. Service ended no later than the Aug 1940 flood; an undated late-1930s Johnson City list shows Johnson City - Pineola trains #2/#3 'with connection to Boone', which suggests Pineola kept trains into the late 1930s but confirms no year. headway_min 1440 is an ESTIMATE (one train each way on that list); no dated timetable was read.

segments.note: Linville River Railway (ET&WNC system) extension, Montezuma - Linville - Linville Gap - Jestes Siding - Townsend - Foscoe - Shulls Mills - Laurel - Hodge's Gap - Boone. Linville and Linville Gap served the Linville resort / Grandfather Mountain trade. Owned by the Linville River Railway Company - a separate corporation filing its own NC Corporation Commission returns with its own crews - but bought by the Cranberry Iron & Coal / ET&WNC group in April 1913 and run from then as one system with the ET&WNC under identical officers at Johnson City, with through trains Johnson City - Boone (1934 order, trains 1 and 2). Drawn in the ET&WNC colour as the company that ran the trains (Rule 4). Start 1919: the construction train reached Boone Oct 24, 1918, freight and mail followed, and regular passenger trains began May 9, 1919 (Appalachian State collection note; Boone 2021 architectural survey 'the following May'; NCCC 1919 road operated 'Montezuma - Boone'). Montezuma - Shulls Mills opened in 1916 for the W. S. Whiting band mill and LRR passenger-train revenue more than doubled 1916 -> 1917, so passengers may have reached Shulls Mills in 1916/17 - not confirmed, so not drawn; secondary claims of 1916 or 1918 'service to Boone' refer to construction/freight and are not adopted. End: the flood of Aug 13, 1940 'stopped engine nine, on her down trip, and she never returned' (Watauga Democrat retrospective, Dec 4, 1952); the Dec 5, 1940 abandonment hearing estimated $150,000 'to re-establish rail service into Boone'. At its peak the system ran Johnson City - Boone, about 66 mi. headway_min 720 is an ESTIMATE: the undated late-1930s Johnson City list shows about two trains each way (Johnson City - Boone and Johnson City - Pineola with connection to Boone); no dated timetable was read.

segments.note: Linville River Railway under W. M. Ritter (lumber, Columbus OH; officers at Saginaw), Cranberry - Minneapolis - Vale - Newland - Montezuma - Saginaw (renamed Pineola 1914). Built ~1899-1900 (etwncrrhs.org: Ritter 'completed the now Linville River Railway from Cranberry to Pineola, NC in 1900'), successor to Isaac T. Mann's Linville River Railroad (1896). Start: [OPEN] 1909 - the first year passengers are printed. The 1901, 1903 and 1905 NCCC returns give only gross earnings ('Principally hauling lumber for owners', 1901); the 1909 return prints 6,319 revenue passengers ($2,527.60 passenger-train revenue), 1910 7,904, 1912 9,276. 1909 is the first CONFIRMED year, not a known start; the 1906-1908 returns were not checked and might move it earlier - do not extend without evidence. End 1913: sold to the Cranberry Iron & Coal / ET&WNC group in April 1913, after which the same trains are drawn as etwnc-cranberry-montezuma and etwnc-montezuma-pineola (1913 is drawn by both, the year of the sale). Fiscal-year basis of the 1909-1912 returns (year to June 30) not verified page by page. headway_min 1440 is an ESTIMATE (one train a day assumed); not sourced.
